courses.name: Communicative English Skills
courses.description: Freshman course designed to improve English communication skills.

notes.note: Parts of speech are categories of words used in sentences. Common categories include nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, prepositions, conjunctions, and interjections.
A noun is a word that names a person, place, thing, or idea. Examples include student, university, book, and education.
A pronoun is used instead of a noun. Common pronouns include I, you, he, she, it, we, and they.
A verb expresses an action or state. Examples include study, read, write, learn, and become.
The subject and verb should agree in number. A singular subject normally takes a singular verb, while a plural subject takes a plural verb.
The simple present is commonly used for habits, routines, facts, and general truths. Example: Students study every day.
The simple past is used for actions that happened and finished in the past. Example: She studied yesterday.
The simple future is commonly used for actions that will happen in the future. Example: They will study tomorrow.
The present continuous is used for an action happening around the present time. Example: The student is reading a book.
Vocabulary is the collection of words a person knows and uses in communication.
Synonyms are words that have similar or nearly similar meanings. Example: big and large.
Antonyms are words with opposite meanings. Example: hot and cold.
Understanding a word in context means using the surrounding words and sentences to understand its meaning.
The main idea is the central point or most important message of a reading passage.
Supporting details provide information that explains, describes, or supports the main idea.
Reading for specific information means looking for particular facts, names, dates, numbers, or other details.
An inference is a conclusion that a reader makes using information from the text and prior knowledge.
A paragraph is a group of related sentences that develops one main idea.
A topic sentence introduces the main idea of a paragraph.
Supporting sentences explain and develop the main idea introduced by the topic sentence.
A concluding sentence brings the paragraph to a logical ending.
Active listening requires paying attention to the speaker and understanding the message.
Listening for the main idea means identifying the most important message in spoken communication.
Listening for details involves identifying specific information from spoken communication.
A clear introduction helps a speaker begin communication and establish the topic.
A discussion involves exchanging ideas, opinions, and information with other people.
An academic presentation should have a clear introduction, organized main points, and a conclusion.
Academic language is formal language commonly used in university study, assignments, presentations, and academic discussions.
Academic discussion requires students to express ideas clearly, listen to others, and provide relevant reasons or evidence.
An academic presentation should be organized, clear, relevant, and appropriate for the audience.

courses.name: Critical Thinking
courses.description: Freshman course focused on reasoning, analysis, problem solving, and decision making.

notes.note: Critical thinking is the process of carefully analyzing information, evaluating ideas, and making reasoned judgments.
Critical thinking helps students evaluate information, solve problems, make decisions, and avoid unsupported conclusions.
An argument is a set of statements in which reasons are presented to support a conclusion.
A premise is a statement that provides support or a reason for a conclusion.
A conclusion is the claim or judgment that an argument attempts to support.
Evidence is information used to support a claim or conclusion.
Reliable evidence should come from trustworthy sources and should be relevant to the claim being evaluated.
Problem solving begins by clearly identifying and understanding the problem.
After identifying a problem, different possible solutions can be developed and evaluated.
Solutions should be evaluated according to their advantages, disadvantages, feasibility, and possible consequences.
Decision making involves choosing among alternatives based on available information and relevant criteria.
Good decision making considers both immediate and possible future consequences.
A logical fallacy is an error in reasoning that can make an argument weak or misleading.
An ad hominem argument attacks a person instead of addressing the person's argument.
A hasty generalization occurs when a broad conclusion is made from insufficient evidence.
